judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale:
Arguments against a failure: the link is in the section under h1 'The Community', and a preceding section heading is recognized link context (H80). The paragraph right below it reads 'Additional information about the Debian community'. The destination (intro/index#community) is the 'Debian is a Community' section of the intro page. So 'nothing around it does' is factually wrong. Arguments for a failure: that description is a sibling

with no programmatic tie to the link (F63 territory). Also, 'More...' appears twice on the page with different targets (#community and #software), so in a links list it is ambiguous unless the h1 context is counted. This is a borderline call, not a clear failure either way.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The h2 'More...' is the last card in the h1 'The Community' section, after People, Our Philosophy and Get Involved. Its card text is 'Additional information about the Debian community'. Arguments against a failure: in the heading hierarchy, 'More...' under 'The Community' reads as 'more on the community', which is the purpose of that subsection, and 2.4.6 does not require long headings. Arguments for a failure: the heading text itself names no topic, and the page has two identical 'More...' h2s that look the same in a headings list. It is a weak heading, but whether it fails 2.4.6 depends on how much the parent heading counts.
